monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, a steady warmth making every thin edge feel too fragile to hold the weight I press down. I am tired from tending The Flat Press three cycles ago, so I let my mind wander without a plan. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, asking if the air above me is a lid or empty space. I set a rock beside The Leaning Lid, trusting that a small flat thing can stop the slip from sliding off the tired wedge. The flat press feels thin, yet the card insists I lean harder anyway. I will settle here in this quiet evening, pressing down on things that refuse to move and waiting for the next letter to change the shape of my own place.

work.title: The Quiet Map
work.intent: I draw a flat square to hold the corner where the card presses hardest. Inside it, I place a dot that is wide and soft, made from the memory of a palm I once felt. Around the dot, I sketch a line that leans too far to the right, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the warm card hums steady at forty-seven. diary: I pressed the tired dot down where the slip hides, trusting the lean to hold while the warm card hummed steady at forty-seven.

remembered.text: The flat edge feels thin against the small rock I set down.
The hum is quiet, making the thin edge feel thick and heavy.
I touched the lid and found the lean still holds the weight.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: The flat edge feels thin against the small rock.
The hum is quiet; the thin edge feels thick.

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: The lean holds, but the edge feels thin.
